messages:
emily: Customer reported truncated SSE output + duplicate billing after a reconnect. Happens when their auth token rotates mid-stream. They said the client reconnects and then gets both the resumed partial output and a full regenerated response — billed twice. Repro steps from customer attached.
sam: Can you paste the repro steps here? which SDK/language? :thinking:
mike: Sounds like resume token got invalidated during auth rotation. Client probably falls back to starting a new generation while server replays remaining chunks — two completions emitted. We saw similar but not identical behavior before. Do we have logs for that session id?
emily: Attaching customer repro notes: "1) open SSE with session_id=abc123; 2) rotate auth token on server after ~6s; 3) client reconnects with old session cookie and new auth header; 4) client receives leftover chunks then a new completion; billing shows two full generations". They used our JS SDK v0.7.2 (non-streaming fallback code path present).
eng-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-472 — tagging eng-runtime and support for triage.
jess: Quick ask: does the server reject reconnects when token rotated? If reconnect accepted but resume token mismatch we should send a resume-mismatch event and not re-run generation. Ideally client should call resume endpoint only if server answers with ok-to-resume.
mike: Implementation detail: current flow accepts socket upgrade if auth header valid, then attempts to find session by session_id. If the session's resume_token != client-provided token we currently fall back to sending remaining buffered tokens and ALSO enqueue a new generation if client requests full start. Edge case: client simultaneously triggers resume and start because of SDK race.
sam: Can we reproduce locally? emily, can you share exact timeline + headers they used? customer included curl snippet. I'll paste minimal repro below.
emily: curl snippet from customer:

```
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?session_id=abc123"
# mid-stream, customer swaps token to NEW_TOKEN, then reconnects:
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?session_id=abc123&resume_token=XYZ"
```

mike: Thanks. Reproduced locally when I force token rotate and simulate a reconnection within the server grace window. Root cause: resume token verification race + client SDK issuing both resume and start in quick succession when it sees partial response timeouts.
jess: Short-term mitigation: support can instruct customer to delete session_id (force a new session) if they see duplicate completions. Also issue a billing credit while we root-cause.
support-bot: Customer ticket updated: CRT-8382 — advised temporary workaround (drop session_id / wait 10s after rotation). Billing team notified for credit review. :white_check_mark:
mike: Medium-term fix suggestions:
- Make server return explicit SSE control event on reconnect: `event: resume-status` with `data: {"status":"ok"}` or `{"status":"invalid"}` so clients can deterministically decide to resume vs start.
- Harden SDK: don't auto-start a new generation if resume-token check hasn't returned `ok`.
- On auth rotation, invalidate resume tokens atomically and force reconnects to receive `invalid` so no replay happens.
jess: Agreed. I'll file a runtime PR to add the `resume-status` control event and update the JS SDK flow to await that event before re-requesting generation. Putting this on the short-term sprint.
emily: Customer reply: they can test workaround now; asked if we can proactively credit both duplicate charges if they occurred. I've asked billing.
sam: Assigning follow-ups: @mike implement server control event (PR), @jess update SDK behavior, @support-bot track billing credit. I'll create a short postmortem note after fixes land.
eng-bot: Linked PRs and follow-ups: https://git.internal/repo/RED-1234, https://git.internal/repo/RED-1235
support-bot: Ticket CRT-8382 updated with expected ETA: SDK fix in next minor, runtime fix in this sprint.
emily: Thanks team — keeping customer updated. :pray:
